findings.title: The 'retired' laptop Facebook monitor is still loaded and running on this Mac, replaying a logged-in session from the house IP with its proxy unset
findings.location: launchd gui/501/com.recycleservers.fbmonitor (pid 14535, KeepAlive, runs=3, started 2026-10-30 05:30) -> ~/Projects/recycle_servers/facebook_tracker/scripts/run-monitor.sh:16; configs/master.toml:15,37-40; scripts/watchdog.sh:14-22
findings.evidence: launchctl list shows com.recycleservers.fbmonitor loaded with live pid 14535 (aimm + playwright driver + chrome-headless-shell children). watchdog.sh:14-22 says the laptop deployment 'has been retired' and that loading it 'would put a SECOND monitor on the same Facebook account from the same public IP ... the single pattern most likely to get the account checkpointed'. logs/monitor.out.log has ~2,000-2,600 lines/day 2026-10-17..10-26 and real searches with results on 10-27 ('4 new listings for server_ram', 10:27:22) and 10-28; ai-marketplace-monitor.log.1 (10-29) is full of AI-Prompt/AI-Response for listings it fetched. master.toml:15 authenticates from configs/sessions/personal.json and :37-40 routes through ${PROXY_HOMELAB}, but monitor.err.log/search-probe.err.log repeat 'Environment variable PROXY_HOMELAB is not set — ignored' (secrets.env has no PROXY_HOMELAB line), so every page went out from the house IP although master.toml:33-35 says the session was captured through the proxy and replaying it elsewhere is 'a location change on an existing login'. Since 2026-10-30 10:00 the log reads 'saved session at configs/sessions/personal.json is not valid ... searching resumes on its own once the file changes'. The homelab VM no longer runs rs-monitor at all (docker ps: only rs-fleet-homelab-1..9, coordinator, console, agent).
findings.failure_scenario: The process stays up (KeepAlive) and retries daily at 10:00. The moment personal.json is rewritten (an rs-session capture/check --save-refreshed for that account, or a copy from the fleet), it silently resumes scraping Marketplace from the office NAT IP, unproxied, alongside the 9 fleet workers on the same LAN, which is exactly the double-traffic/location-change pattern the repo's First Rule exists to prevent. The personal.json session already went invalid on 2026-10-29/30 while this was running; this host is a plausible contributor.
findings.proposed_fix: Owner decision: `launchctl bootout gui/501/com.recycleservers.fbmonitor` and move the plist out of ~/Library/LaunchAgents (stopping it is not a login; it closes a browser). Do the same for the watchdog. Do not touch personal.json until it is unloaded.
findings.regression_test: `launchctl list | grep fbmonitor` returns nothing and `pgrep -f chrome-headless-shell` shows no process parented by aimm; add a check to the review checklist that no com.recycleservers.* job references ~/Projects/recycle_servers/facebook_tracker.

findings.title: search-probe opens Marketplace every morning with the personal.json logged-in session, from the house IP, out of the stale legacy checkout
findings.location: launchd gui/501/com.recycleservers.search-probe (07:45 daily, last exit 0, runs=10) -> ~/Projects/recycle_servers/facebook_tracker/scripts/probe-search-url.sh:34; scripts/probe-search-url.py:42,145,165
findings.evidence: probe-search-url.py:42 DEFAULT_SESSION = configs/sessions/personal.json, :165 storage_state=args.session; the header (line 14) says it 'Needs an authenticated session'. The job ran successfully every day through 2026-10-31 07:46 (reports/search-probe-2026-10-31.md: dc search, 16 results, 15 detail pages the monitor would open). Its err log shows the same 'PROXY_HOMELAB is not set — ignored' warnings 45 times and repeated 'Page crashed/Target crashed'. It runs from the legacy JinhuW/facebook_tracker clone last fetched 2026-10-16, not trackers/facebook/.
findings.failure_scenario: A scheduled job nobody watches restores a Facebook session and browses Marketplace from the office IP every day; each run is a session restore of the kind the First Rule counts as a login risk. If personal.json is the same account as a fleet worker (not verified; needs_owner), it is the same account seen from two IPs on the same morning.
findings.proposed_fix: Unload com.recycleservers.search-probe (owner decision), or if the probe is still wanted, port it to trackers/facebook/ and run it logged-out (the logged-out /marketplace/<city>/ resolver from memory fb-city-slug-logged-out-resolver works without a session).
findings.regression_test: launchctl list shows no search-probe job referencing the legacy path; reports/ stops gaining search-probe-<date>.md.

findings.title: keyword-eval has failed every day since 2026-10-25 because the rs-monitor container it reads no longer exists
findings.evidence: eval-keywords.sh:23 C=rs-monitor and :49 ssh's `docker logs --since 24h rs-monitor`. keyword-eval.out.log: last 'done' 2026-10-24 08:05; 2026-10-25..10-31 only 'fetching container log'. keyword-eval.err.log repeats "error: could not read `docker logs rs-monitor` on jinhu@10.10.10.73" daily. `docker ps -a` on 10.10.10.73 lists no rs-monitor (the fleet is rs-fleet-homelab-1..9). The newest report is reports/keywords-2026-10-24.md.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner believes a daily keyword review is produced; none has been for 7 days and nothing alerts (launchd just records exit 1). It also holds a long-lived Claude OAuth token in the legacy checkout for a job that cannot succeed.
findings.proposed_fix: Retire the job (unload plist) or repoint it at the fleet's log source (OpenSearch fb-tracker-* per memory fleet-ai-verdict-logs) from trackers/facebook/. If retired, revoke the .claude-oauth-token in that checkout.
findings.regression_test: After the change, `launchctl print gui/501/com.recycleservers.keyword-eval` shows last exit 0 and a new reports/keywords-<date>.md, or the label is gone.

findings.title: Stale deployable checkouts: five ERP clones at v1.261-1.268, one linked to Railway production, and the legacy facebook_tracker clone with a working deploy.sh
findings.evidence: git survey: recycle_servres_erp (dev, 86f81524, 2026-10-17, v1.268.0, node_modules + deploy/cloudflare/.wrangler present), -dev-2 v1.261.0, -dev-3 v1.266.0 (node_modules), -dev-4 v1.268.0, -main-3 v1.262.0 (node_modules); current is v1.395.0. ~/.railway/config.json links recycle_servers_v2/recycle_servres_erp-handfish (branch fix-sell-order-totals, v1.291.1, last commit 2026-10-19) to recycle-erp-experiment **production**. deploy/cloudflare/deploy.sh has no check that HEAD is current origin/main. The legacy facebook_tracker clone (origin JinhuW/facebook_tracker, archived; last fetch 2026-10-16; 3 modified tracked files) still has scripts/deploy.sh targeting jinhu@10.10.10.73 and rsync --delete. Only reddits_tracker was archived on 2026-10-24 (memory legacy-tracker-checkouts-archived).
findings.failure_scenario: An agent or the owner opens one of these folders (they are still named like the live repo) and runs `railway up` in handfish -> production backend rolled back ~100 versions with migrations missing; or `deploy/cloudflare/deploy.sh` in recycle_servers/recycle_servres_erp -> prod Worker rolled back to v1.268. A deploy.sh from the legacy facebook_tracker clone rsyncs stale code to the homelab VM and restarts containers, i.e. Facebook logins.
findings.proposed_fix: Owner decision: move the five ~/Projects/recycle_servers/recycle_servres_erp* clones, recycle_servers_v2/recycle_servres_erp-{handfish,lancetfish}, and (after B5-01/02/03 are unloaded) ~/Projects/recycle_servers/facebook_tracker into ~/Projects/_archive with a README, and `railway unlink` the handfish path. Optionally add an `origin/main` ancestry guard to deploy/cloudflare/deploy.sh (other lane's file).
findings.regression_test: No path under ~/Projects outside the ERP main clone/worktrees has deploy/cloudflare/deploy.sh; ~/.railway/config.json has no production link to a non-worktree checkout.

findings.title: [cross-lane] memtrade, the far side of the /api/wechat-market/push contract, has no commits and no backup
findings.location: ~/Projects/wehat_ai/memtrade (.git with zero commits; tmutil: no destinations configured)
findings.evidence: `git log` -> "your current branch 'main' does not have any commits yet"; `git status` lists every file (src/, scripts/, deploy/, tests/, package.json) as untracked; no origin remote. `tmutil destinationinfo` -> 'No destinations configured'. AGENTS.md says the ERP side 'has to keep accepting what the deployed memtrade sends', and the deployed memtrade is this working directory (launchd runs src/cli.ts from it). Daily run itself is healthy: daily.out.log shows start/done every day 2026-10-26..10-31, last push 'erp: pushed 2026-10-31 — 623 lines, 2237 points'.
findings.failure_scenario: A disk failure, an accidental `rm`, or an agent edit to src/erp.ts leaves no way to recover or even diff what the ERP contract counterpart sends; the 300 MB data/memtrade.sqlite history is equally unbacked.
findings.proposed_fix: Make an initial commit and push to a private remote (the three token files are 0600 and must be in .gitignore first; verify), and back up data/ (or point R2 backup at it).
findings.regression_test: `git -C ~/Projects/wehat_ai/memtrade log -1` succeeds and `git status --short` does not list src/.

findings.title: Facebook session cookie files in the legacy checkout are world-readable (0644)
findings.evidence: ls -l: personal.json -rw-r--r-- (mtime 2026-10-26), import-*.cookies.json -rw-r--r--; by contrast personal.json.meta.json and secrets.env are 0600. Contents not read.
findings.failure_scenario: Any other local user or process running as another uid can read live Facebook session cookies. Single-user Mac, so low exposure.
findings.proposed_fix: chmod 600 those files (or remove them when the checkout is archived per B5-04). Owner action since it touches a sessions directory.

findings.title: Unauthenticated HTTP servers on 0.0.0.0 with the macOS firewall off serve review docs and WeChat market reports to the whole LAN
findings.location: launchd com.jinhu.archify-previews (python3 -m http.server 8800 --bind 0.0.0.0, ~/archify-previews) and com.wehatai.memtrade-web (node src/cli.ts serve, *:8780)
findings.evidence: lsof: Python 9778 *:8800 LISTEN, node 77636 *:8780 LISTEN. socketfilterfw: 'Firewall is disabled'. ~/archify-previews holds 62 files incl. acl-review-20261031.html, code-review-2026-10-31.html, full-review-prompt.md and account-pool screenshots (rs-475-account-brief.png, rs441-pool-*.png); http.server gives a directory index. /tmp/archify-previews.log shows clients 10.10.100.106 and .225 only. archify server itself healthy (running, never exited).
findings.failure_scenario: Any device on the office network (guest Wi-Fi if not segmented) can list and fetch unfixed security findings and fleet account screenshots, or the WeChat price reports, with no credentials.
findings.proposed_fix: Bind to the VPN/LAN interface the owner uses or put a basic-auth/allowlist in front; keep sensitive reviews out of ~/archify-previews; enable the application firewall.
findings.regression_test: From another LAN host, curl http://<mac>:8800/ returns 401/connection refused unless from the allowlisted address.

findings.title: fbmonitor watchdog pkills every chrome-headless-shell on the Mac
findings.evidence: `pkill -f "ai_marketplace_monitor|/aimm "` and `pkill -f "chrome-headless-shell"` when ~/.ai-marketplace-monitor/ai-marketplace-monitor.log is >110 min stale; it fired on 2026-08-20 and 2026-10-07 (logs/watchdog.log). Because B5-01's monitor is loaded, the guard at :45 passes.
findings.failure_scenario: If the monitor log stalls (e.g. the Mac sleeps), the watchdog kills every Playwright headless browser on the machine, including other sessions' e2e runs, and then reloads the retired monitor (B5-01).
findings.proposed_fix: Goes away with unloading the watchdog per B5-01; otherwise kill only descendants of the agent's pid.
